subproblems.title: C¹ push-forward of an integer multiplicity triple carried by a compact set is a current supported in the image
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n), K ⊆ U compact with Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), O ⊆ ℝ^P open with K ⊆ O, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on O with f(K) ⊆ U. Then there is Q ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) with Q(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), where Df(x) = fderiv ℝ f x and (α∘L)(v₁, …, vₙ) = α(Lv₁, …, Lvₙ) (α.compContinuousLinearMap L); moreover spt Q is compact and spt Q ⊆ f(K). This is f_#τ(M, θ, ξ) of Simon Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24(2).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K O : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ K) = 0 → IsOpen O → K ⊆ O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → f '' K ⊆ U → ∃ Q : GeometricCurrentOn U n, (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Q ω = ∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∂μHE[n]) ∧ IsCompact Q.support ∧ Q.support ⊆ f '' K
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5(a)–(b) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24(2), chapter-06.txt lines 403–440), specialized to a compact set K in place of F = B̄_t(y), the open set O in place of B_r(y), and a general f in place of π. The hypothesis Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 replaces the parent's step 2(a) ("μ_X is carried by F").
Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; μ := Hⁿ⌞M. ‖·‖ denotes operator norms (of linear maps, of n-covectors as continuous alternating maps, and of n-vectors as functionals on n-covectors). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) put β_ω(x) := ω(f(x))∘Df(x) (= (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) and ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_z ‖ω(z)‖, which is finite because ω is continuous with compact support.
1. Derivative bound. Since f is C¹ on the open set O, f and x ↦ Df(x) are continuous on O (Mathlib ContDiffOn.continuousOn, ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen). K ⊆ O is compact, so Λ_K := sup_{x∈K} ‖Df(x)‖ < ∞ (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn; take Λ_K := 0 if K = ∅).
2. Pointwise bound. For every n-covector α and linear L, ‖α∘L‖ ≤ ‖α‖·‖L‖ⁿ (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_compContinuousLinearMap_le). Hence ‖β_ω(x)‖ ≤ ‖ω‖_∞·Λ_Kⁿ for every x ∈ K.
3. Orientation bound. By the field R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there are an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) and s ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(x)(β) = s·β(τ) for every n-covector β. At such x, |ξ(x)(β)| = |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖·Π_i|τ_i| = ‖β‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm). (This is the content of the accepted DAG declaration dpf_pfc_imrep_orient_abs_apply_le; a decomposition of this node may reuse it.)
4. Measurability. On O the map x ↦ β_ω(x) is continuous (ω, f and Df are continuous there, and (α, L) ↦ α∘L is continuous), so x ↦ 1_K(x)·β_ω(x) is Borel. Since μ(ℝ^P ∖ K) = Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 (M is Borel), the integrand x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(β_ω(x)) agrees μ-a.e. with x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(1_K(x)β_ω(x)), which is μ-a.e. strongly measurable: θ is Borel, ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and evaluation (ζ, β) ↦ ζ(β) is continuous.
5. Integrability and the basic estimate. By steps 2–4, |θ(x)ξ(x)(β_ω(x))| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞·Λ_Kⁿ·θ(x)·1_K(x) for μ-a.e. x, and c_K := ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult (K is compact and K ⊆ U). So the integrand is μ-integrable, and I(ω) := ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(β_ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) satisfies |I(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞·Λ_Kⁿ·c_K. (Accepted DAG declaration dpf_pfc_imrep_pairing_integrable_abs_le has exactly this form with C := K and F := 1_K·β_ω.)
6. Linearity. β_{aω+bη}(x) = a·β_ω(x) + b·β_η(x) for a, b ∈ ℝ, because evaluation at f(x) is linear and α ↦ α∘L is linear. As ξ(x) is linear and all integrands are integrable (step 5), I(aω + bη) = a·I(ω) + b·I(η). So I is a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U).
7. Continuity. Let ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U), i.e. TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0: there is a compact C ⊆ U with tsupport ω_j ⊆ C for all j, and the k = 0 clause says ω_j → 0 uniformly on C (iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j is ω_j composed with the norm-preserving curry0 equivalence). Since ω_j = 0 off C, ‖ω_j‖_∞ → 0 (accepted DAG declaration dpf_pfc_testFormOnConverges_zero_uniform). By step 5, |I(ω_j)| ≤ ‖ω_j‖_∞·Λ_Kⁿ·c_K → 0. Hence Q := I is a GeometricCurrentOn U n, and Q(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
8. Vanishing away from f(K). Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ∩ f(K) = ∅. For x ∈ K, f(x) ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(f(x)) = 0 and β_ω(x) = 0. The integrand vanishes on M ∩ K, hence μ-a.e. (Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0), and Q(ω) = 0.
9. Support. f is continuous on K, so f(K) is compact, hence closed; and f(K) ⊆ U by hypothesis. Let z ∈ U ∖ f(K). Since U ∖ f(K) is open, there is s > 0 with closedBall(z, s) ⊆ U ∖ f(K). The ball W := ball(z, s) is open, closure W = closedBall(z, s) (s ≠ 0) is compact and contained in U, and Q vanishes on W: if tsupport ω ⊆ W then tsupport ω ∩ f(K) = ∅, so Q(ω) = 0 by step 8. Thus W belongs to the family whose union is the zero region of Q (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.zeroRegion), z ∈ zeroRegion(Q), and z ∉ spt Q = U ∖ zeroRegion(Q). As spt Q ⊆ U by definition, spt Q ⊆ f(K).
10. Compactness. From spt Q = U ∖ zeroRegion(Q), spt Q ⊆ f(K) and f(K) ⊆ U we get spt Q = f(K) ∖ zeroRegion(Q) = f(K) ∩ (zeroRegion Q)ᶜ. The zero region is open (a union of open sets), so spt Q is a closed subset of the compact set f(K), hence compact. ∎
proof_key_steps: Df is continuous on O, so ‖Df‖ ≤ Λ_K on the compact K; unit orientations satisfy |ξ(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ and ‖α∘L‖ ≤ ‖α‖‖L‖ⁿ.
Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 makes the integrand a.e. equal to a bounded Borel integrand supported in M ∩ K, so it is integrable with |Q(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞Λ_Kⁿ∫_{M∩K}θ.
Linearity is pointwise; test-form convergence forces ‖ω_j‖_∞ → 0, giving sequential continuity, so Q is a GeometricCurrentOn U n.
Forms vanishing on the compact f(K) give Q = 0, so every point of U ∖ f(K) has a ball in the zero region: spt Q ⊆ f(K).
spt Q = f(K) minus the open zero region is a closed subset of the compact f(K), hence compact.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5(c) of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 6, 3.3–3.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 770–860), with the correction stated in the parent: Simon's multiplicity N in 3.8 is only a non-negative integer (oppositely oriented sheets with the same image cancel; e.g. an oriented rectangle boundary projected onto a line has zero push-forward), so the carrier is restricted to {N ≥ 1}. Also used: Simon Ch. 3, 1.1–1.6 and 2.6 (chapter-03.txt lines 1–143 and 330–410) and the tangent-locality statement (TL) assumed in the hypothesis. Here K, O and f play the roles of F = B̄_t(y), B_r(y) and π, and Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 replaces the parent's step 2(a).
Deviation from the parent, for formalizability (the mathematics is the same): the parent's step 5(c2) obtains the injectivity pieces from C¹ submanifolds N_j covering M, i.e. from the "only if" half of Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2, which the pinned SimonGMT library does not contain (Chapter03/SubmanifoldCover.lean proves only the converse). Step 2 below obtains the pieces instead from Lipschitz parametrizations, SimonGMT's regular-set lemmas and Mathlib's partition lemma exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt (the same construction proves the accepted DAG declaration dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces, which a decomposition of this node may reuse). The approximate tangent planes of the image pieces, which the parent reads off from the C¹ image submanifolds Σ_k, are supplied by Lemma T below. Steps 3–9 are the parent's (c3)–(c9).
Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). M_R := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient. Λⁿ denotes the n-covectors and Λ_n := MultiVector P n the n-vectors of ℝ^P. For increasing I = (i₁ < ⋯ < iₙ) let dx^I(v₁, …, vₙ) := det[(v_j)_{i_k}]_{k,j} and e_I := (e_{i₁}, …, e_{iₙ}); every n-covector satisfies α = Σ_I α(e_I)dx^I (multilinearity and the alternating property), so the coordinates ζ(dx^I) determine ζ ∈ Λ_n. Put |α|_E := (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} and |ζ| := (Σ_I ζ(dx^I)²)^{1/2}. For a linear L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P and ζ ∈ Λ_n let L_#ζ ∈ Λ_n, (L_#ζ)(α) := ζ(α∘L); then (L₁L₂)_# = (L₁)_#(L₂)_#. For a linear A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P let A_#e ∈ Λ_n, (A_#e)(α) := α(Ae₁, …, Aeₙ) (e the standard basis of ℝⁿ), and J_A := det(⟨Ae_i, Ae_j⟩)^{1/2} (= normDet A). For g : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P differentiable at a, J_g(a) := J_{Dg(a)} (SimonGMT areaJacobianAt).
Multilinear facts (the parent's (L1)–(L4), with proofs).
 (L1) For v₁, …, vₙ ∈ ℝ^P: α(v) = Σ_I α(e_I)·det[(v_j)_I] (expand α = Σ_I α(e_I)dx^I), and Σ_I det[(v_j)_I]² = det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩) (Cauchy–Binet). By Cauchy–Schwarz, |α(v)| ≤ |α|_E·det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)^{1/2}. Hadamard's inequality det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩) ≤ Π_j|v_j|² (Gram–Schmidt: for independent v, v_j = Σ_{i≤j} R_{ij}σ_i with σ orthonormal, det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩) = Π_j R_{jj}² and |R_{jj}| ≤ |v_j|; for dependent v the determinant is 0) gives |α(v)| ≤ |α|_E·Π_j|v_j|. Also |α(v)| ≤ ‖α‖·Π_j|v_j| (operator norm).
 (L2) For every ζ ∈ Λ_n and α: ζ(α) = Σ_I α(e_I)ζ(dx^I), so |ζ(α)| ≤ |ζ|·|α|_E (Cauchy–Schwarz). If ζ(α) = ±α(τ) with τ orthonormal, then |ζ|² = Σ_I det[(τ_j)_I]² = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = 1 (Cauchy–Binet), so |ζ| = 1.
 (L3) Let ζ(α) = ±α(τ) and ζ'(α) = ±α(σ) for orthonormal bases τ, σ of the same n-plane. Then τ_j = Σ_i O_{ij}σ_i with O := (⟨σ_i, τ_j⟩) orthogonal, so α(τ) = det(O)·α(σ) with det O = ±1 (multilinear alternating expansion), and ζ' = ±ζ.
 (L4) Let ζ(α) = s·α(τ) (s = ±1) for an orthonormal basis τ of an n-plane P₀, and L linear. Then (L_#ζ)(α) = s·α(Lτ₁, …, Lτₙ), and by (L2)'s computation |L_#ζ| = det(⟨Lτ_i, Lτ_j⟩)^{1/2} ≤ Π_i|Lτ_i| ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ (Hadamard). If |L_#ζ| = 0 then (Lτ_i) is dependent and L_#ζ = 0 (alternating). If |L_#ζ| > 0 then L is injective on P₀, L(P₀) is an n-plane with orthonormal basis σ, Lτ_j = Σ_l B_{lj}σ_l, (L_#ζ)(α) = s·det(B)·α(σ) by (L3)'s expansion, and |det B| = |L_#ζ|; so L_#ζ/|L_#ζ| is a unit orientation of L(P₀). The same computation with τ replaced by the standard basis e of ℝⁿ shows: for injective A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, |A_#e| = J_A > 0 and A_#e/J_A is a unit orientation of range A.
0. Set-up and cutoff.
 (a) M := M_R ∩ K is Borel (K is compact, hence closed). It is countably n-rectifiable (subset of M_R; SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono). As θ ≥ 1 on M_R, Hⁿ(M) ≤ ∫_M θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult with K). Since Hⁿ(M_R ∖ K) = 0, Q(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x) for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
 (b) Choose an open V with K ⊆ V and closure V compact and contained in O, and χ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P), 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, with tsupport χ ⊆ V and χ = 1 on an open set W₀ ⊇ K. Put f̂ := χ·f (0 off tsupport χ). Then f̂ is C¹ on ℝ^P (C¹ on O, identically 0 near each point of the open set ℝ^P ∖ tsupport χ, and these two open sets cover ℝ^P); its derivative is continuous with compact support, so f̂ is L̂-Lipschitz on ℝ^P for some L̂ (mean value inequality). On W₀, f̂ = f; hence f̂(x) = f(x) and Df̂(x) = Df(x) for x ∈ K. So Q(ω) = ∫_M θξ(ω(f̂(x))∘Df̂(x)) dHⁿ, f̂(K) = f(K) ⊆ U, and Λ := max(1, sup_{x∈K}‖Df(x)‖) < ∞ bounds ‖Df̂‖ on K. From now on we write f for f̂.
1. Orientation and Jacobian.
 (a) Fix a Borel map ξ̃ : ℝ^P → Λ_n with ξ̃ = ξ Hⁿ-a.e. on M_R (ξ is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M_R and Λ_n is finite-dimensional).
 (b) Call x ∈ M oriented if M has an approximate tangent space T_xM at x (unique, SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) and ξ̃(x) is a unit orientation of T_xM. Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M is oriented: by R.orients, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_R there is Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_R x Q_x and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q_x, and ξ(x) = ξ̃(x); by (TL) with (U, A, B) := (U, M, M_R) (M ⊆ M_R ⊆ U Borel; Hⁿ(M_R ∩ K₀) < ∞ for compact K₀ ⊆ U since θ ≥ 1), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M the sets M and M_R have the same approximate tangent spaces at x.
 (c) J(x) := |(Df(x))_#ξ̃(x)| is Borel (Df continuous, ξ̃ Borel, (L, ζ) ↦ L_#ζ continuous). At an oriented x ∈ M, by (L4): J(x) ≤ ‖Df(x)‖ⁿ ≤ Λⁿ; J(x) > 0 iff Df(x) is injective on T_xM; and J(x) = 0 implies (Df(x))_#ξ̃(x) = 0. Put M₊ := {x ∈ M : J(x) > 0}, a Borel set.
Lemma T (approximate tangent planes along bi-Lipschitz pieces; Simon Ch. 3, 1.5–1.6 for a Lipschitz parametrization). Let g : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be Lipschitz, D ⊆ ℝⁿ Borel, c > 0 with |g(a) − g(a')| ≥ c|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ D, and g differentiable at every a ∈ D with Dg(a) injective. Let Y ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel with g(D) ⊆ Y and Hⁿ(Y ∩ K₀) < ∞ for every compact K₀. Then for Lⁿ-a.e. a ∈ D, Y has approximate tangent space Π_a := range Dg(a) at g(a).
 Proof. (i) g is injective on D, so g(D) is Borel (Lusin–Souslin, Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn) and Hⁿ(g(D) ∩ K₀) < ∞. (ii) Lⁿ-a.e. a ∈ D is a Lebesgue density point of D and a Lebesgue point of the bounded Borel function 1_D·J_g (Lebesgue differentiation theorem). Fix such an a, put x := g(a), and let f₀ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f₀ ⊆ B_ρ(0). For λ > 0, with η_{x,λ}(z) := λ⁻¹(z − x), the scaling of Hⁿ under similarities, the area formula for the injective Lipschitz map g on D (SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn) and the substitution b = a + λu give
  ∫_{η_{x,λ}(g(D))} f₀ dHⁿ = λ⁻ⁿ∫_{g(D)} f₀(λ⁻¹(z − x)) dHⁿ(z) = ∫_{(D−a)/λ} f₀(λ⁻¹(g(a + λu) − g(a)))·J_g(a + λu) du.
 If a + λu ∈ D and the integrand is non-zero, then cλ|u| ≤ |g(a + λu) − g(a)| < λρ, so |u| < ρ/c. As λ ↓ 0, λ⁻¹(g(a + λu) − g(a)) → Dg(a)u uniformly for |u| ≤ ρ/c (differentiability at a), so the f₀-factor converges uniformly there (f₀ is uniformly continuous), while ∫_{B_{ρ/c}(0)} |1_{(D−a)/λ}(u)J_g(a + λu) − J_g(a)| du → 0 (Lebesgue point). Hence the integral tends to J_g(a)∫_{B_{ρ/c}(0)} f₀(Dg(a)u) du = J_g(a)∫_{ℝⁿ} f₀(Dg(a)u) du = ∫_{Π_a} f₀ dHⁿ (area formula for the injective linear map Dg(a), whose Jacobian is J_g(a)); here f₀(Dg(a)u) = 0 for |u| ≥ ρ/c because |Dg(a)u| ≥ c|u|, which follows from the lower bound at the density point a. Thus g(D) has approximate tangent space Π_a at g(a) for Lⁿ-a.e. a ∈ D. (iii) By (TL) with (U, A, B) := (ℝ^P, g(D), Y), for Hⁿ-a.e. z ∈ g(D) the sets g(D) and Y have the same approximate tangent spaces at z. The inverse of g on g(D) is (1/c)-Lipschitz, so the set of a ∈ D with g(a) in this Hⁿ-null exceptional set is Lⁿ-null. Combining with (ii) proves the lemma. ∎
Partition step (P). Let g : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P and let G ⊆ ℝⁿ be a Borel set such that g is differentiable at every a ∈ G with Dg(a) injective. For injective linear A put m(A) := min_{|h|=1}|Ah| > 0 (n ≥ 1, so the unit sphere is compact and non-empty) and r(A) := m(A)/2; put r(A) := 1 for non-injective A. Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt (applied with f' := Dg, which is a derivative within G at points of G) gives pairwise disjoint Borel sets t_l (l ∈ ℕ) with G ⊆ ⋃_l t_l and linear maps A_l with |g(a) − g(a') − A_l(a − a')| ≤ r(A_l)|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ G ∩ t_l, where A_l = Dg(y_l) for some y_l ∈ G when G ≠ ∅ (so A_l is injective). Hence |g(a) − g(a')| ≥ |A_l(a − a')| − (m(A_l)/2)|a − a'| ≥ (m(A_l)/2)|a − a'| on G ∩ t_l: g is injective on G ∩ t_l with a (2/m(A_l))-Lipschitz inverse.
2. Injective pieces.
 (a) Lipschitz parametrizations of M. By CountablyRectifiable n M there are an Hⁿ-null M₀ and Lipschitz F'_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F'_j(ℝⁿ). Let G'_j := {a : F'_j differentiable at a, DF'_j(a) injective} (SimonGMT areaRegularSet F'_j, Borel by measurableSet_areaRegularSet); Hⁿ(F'_j(ℝⁿ ∖ G'_j)) = 0 (SimonGMT area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero). Apply (P) to F'_j on G'_j and enumerate the resulting pieces over all j as (F_i, B_i)_{i∈ℕ}, intersecting with F_i⁻¹(M): F_i is one of the Lipschitz F'_j, B_i ⊆ G'_j ∩ F_i⁻¹(M) is Borel, F_i is differentiable with injective DF_i(a) at every a ∈ B_i, |F_i(a) − F_i(a')| ≥ m_i|a − a'| on B_i for some m_i > 0, F_i(B_i) ⊆ M, and M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i) ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F'_j(ℝⁿ ∖ G'_j) is Hⁿ-null.
 (b) By Lemma T with (g, D, Y) := (F_i, B_i, M): for Lⁿ-a.e. a ∈ B_i, T_{F_i(a)}M = range DF_i(a).
 (c) g_i := f∘F_i is Lipschitz; for a ∈ B_i it is differentiable at a with Dg_i(a) = Df(F_i(a))∘DF_i(a) (chain rule). G_i := {a ∈ B_i : Dg_i(a) injective} is Borel (a ↦ Dg_i(a) is Borel, Mathlib measurable_fderiv, and injectivity means det(⟨Dg_i(a)e_p, Dg_i(a)e_q⟩) ≠ 0).
 (d) Apply (P) to g_i on G_i: Borel pieces D_{i,l} ⊆ G_i (disjoint in l, covering G_i) on which g_i is injective with Lipschitz inverse.
 (e) Enumerate the pairs (i, l) as k ∈ ℕ and write F_k, m_k for the parametrization F_i and constant m_i of the pair, and g_k := f∘F_k. Put D'_k := D_{i,l} ∩ F_k⁻¹(M₊) (Borel), A'_k := F_k(D'_k) ⊆ M₊ (Borel by Lusin–Souslin, F_k being continuous and injective on B_i ⊇ D'_k), and disjointify: A_k := A'_k ∖ ⋃_{k'<k} A'_{k'} (Borel, pairwise disjoint, ⋃_k A_k = ⋃_k A'_k), D''_k := D'_k ∩ F_k⁻¹(A_k) (Borel), so A_k = F_k(D''_k). f is injective on A_k: f(F_k(a)) = f(F_k(a')) with a, a' ∈ D''_k means g_k(a) = g_k(a'), so a = a'. Moreover g_k has a Lipschitz inverse on D''_k, and Σ_k := f(A_k) = g_k(D''_k) is Borel (Lusin–Souslin) with Hⁿ(Σ_k) ≤ L̂ⁿHⁿ(A_k) < ∞.
 (f) Hⁿ(M₊ ∖ ⋃_k A_k) = 0. Indeed, let x ∈ M₊ be oriented with x = F_i(a), a ∈ B_i and T_xM = range DF_i(a). Then J(x) > 0, so Df(x) is injective on T_xM = range DF_i(a) (1(c)), hence Dg_i(a) = Df(x)DF_i(a) is injective, a ∈ G_i ⊆ ⋃_l D_{i,l}, and x ∈ A'_k ⊆ ⋃_k A_k for some k. The remaining points of M₊ lie in M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i), in the non-oriented null set, or in F_i(N_i) with N_i ⊆ B_i Lⁿ-null from (b); F_i(N_i) is Hⁿ-null because F_i is Lipschitz (Mathlib LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le).
 (g) By Lemma T with (g, D, Y) := (g_k, D''_k, Σ_k): for Lⁿ-a.e. a ∈ D''_k, Σ_k has approximate tangent space range Dg_k(a) = Df(F_k(a))(range DF_k(a)) at f(F_k(a)).
3. Compact pieces and the image set.
 (a) Hⁿ⌞M is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, hence inner regular. For each k choose pairwise disjoint compact K_{k,1}, K_{k,2}, … ⊆ A_k with Hⁿ(A_k ∖ ⋃_l K_{k,l}) = 0. Enumerate all K_{k,l} as K₁, K₂, … with K_m ⊆ A_{k(m)}; they are pairwise disjoint. M' := ⋃_m K_m ⊆ M₊ is Borel and Hⁿ(M₊ ∖ M') = 0.
 (b) E := f(M') = ⋃_m f(K_m) is σ-compact, hence Borel; E ⊆ f(K) ⊆ U and Hⁿ(E) ≤ L̂ⁿHⁿ(M) < ∞. As f|K_m is a continuous injection of a compact set, x_m := (f|K_m)⁻¹ : f(K_m) → K_m is continuous.
 (c) Countable rectifiability: by 2(a), E ⊆ f(M) ⊆ f(M₀) ∪ ⋃_j (f∘F'_j)(ℝⁿ), where Hⁿ(f(M₀)) ≤ L̂ⁿ·0 = 0 and every f∘F'_j is Lipschitz. Hence every subset of E is countably n-rectifiable.
 (d) Good points. Call x ∈ M' good if x is oriented and, with m such that x ∈ K_m, k := k(m) and a ∈ D''_k with F_k(a) = x: T_xM = range DF_k(a) and Σ_k has approximate tangent space Df(x)(T_xM) at f(x). By 1(b), 2(b), 2(g), and since F_k maps Lⁿ-null sets to Hⁿ-null sets, Hⁿ(M' ∖ good) = 0. Conversely, the set of a ∈ D''_k with F_k(a) ∈ M' ∖ good is Lⁿ-null (F_k has a (1/m_k)-Lipschitz inverse on F_k(D''_k)).
4. Area formula. Fix m, k := k(m), D_m := D''_k ∩ F_k⁻¹(K_m) (Borel), so F_k(D_m) = K_m and g_k(D_m) = f(K_m). For a ∈ D_m with x := F_k(a) good: σ := (DF_k(a))_#e/J_{DF_k(a)} is a unit orientation of range DF_k(a) = T_xM (L4), so σ = ±ξ̃(x) (L3), and J_{g_k}(a) = |(Df(x)DF_k(a))_#e| = |(Df(x))_#((DF_k(a))_#e)| = J_{F_k}(a)·|(Df(x))_#σ| = J_{F_k}(a)·J(x), using (L∘A)_#e = L_#(A_#e) (both send α to α(LAe₁, …, LAeₙ)) and (L4). For Borel h ≥ 0, the area formula for the injective Lipschitz maps F_k and g_k on D_m (SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn) gives
  ∫_{K_m} h·J dHⁿ = ∫_{D_m} J_{F_k}(a)·h(F_k(a))·J(F_k(a)) da = ∫_{D_m} J_{g_k}(a)·h(F_k(a)) da = ∫_{f(K_m)} h(x_m(w)) dHⁿ(w),
 using x_m(g_k(a)) = F_k(a) and 3(d) for the a.e. identity of Jacobians. Summing over m (monotone convergence; the K_m are disjoint and f is injective on each):
 (A) ∫_{M'} h·J dHⁿ = ∫ Σ_m 1_{f(K_m)}(w)·h(x_m(w)) dHⁿ(w) = ∫ Σ_{x∈f⁻¹(w)∩M'} h(x) dHⁿ(w).
 Each point of f⁻¹(w) ∩ M' lies in exactly one K_m and equals x_m(w), which gives the last equality; the integrand is Borel. With h := θ: ∫ Σ_{x∈f⁻¹(w)∩M'} θ(x) dHⁿ(w) = ∫_{M'} θJ dHⁿ ≤ Λⁿ∫_M θ dHⁿ < ∞. So the Borel set E₁ := {w : Σ_{x∈f⁻¹(w)∩M'} θ(x) < ∞} has Hⁿ(ℝ^P ∖ E₁) = 0, and for w ∈ E₁ the fibre f⁻¹(w) ∩ M' is finite (θ ≥ 1).
5. The image integral.
 (a) ζ̂(x) := J(x)⁻¹·(Df(x))_#ξ̃(x) for x ∈ M' and ζ̂(x) := 0 otherwise. ζ̂ is Borel, |ζ̂| = 1 on M', and at good x, ζ̂(x) is a unit orientation of Df(x)(T_xM) (L4).
 (b) V(w) := Σ_m 1_{f(K_m)}(w)·θ(x_m(w))·ζ̂(x_m(w)) = Σ_{x∈f⁻¹(w)∩M'} θ(x)ζ̂(x) for w ∈ E₁, and V(w) := 0 for w ∉ E₁. The series converges absolutely on E₁ because |ζ̂(x)(dx^I)| ≤ |ζ̂(x)| = 1; each coordinate V(·)(dx^I) is Borel, so V is Borel.
 (c) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M (oriented, ξ(x) = ξ̃(x)): θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) = θ(x)((Df(x))_#ξ̃(x))(ω(f(x))), which is 0 for x ∈ M ∖ M₊ (1(c)) and equals θ(x)J(x)ζ̂(x)(ω(f(x))) for x ∈ M'. As Hⁿ(M₊ ∖ M') = 0: Q(ω) = ∫_{M'} θ(x)J(x)ζ̂(x)(ω(f(x))) dHⁿ(x). Apply (A) to the positive and negative parts of h(x) := θ(x)ζ̂(x)(ω(f(x))); both have finite integral against J, since |h| ≤ θ·sup_z|ω(z)|_E (L2) and ∫_{M'} θJ < ∞. On the fibre over w we have f(x) = w, so
 (B) Q(ω) = ∫ V(w)(ω(w)) dHⁿ(w).
6. Tangent planes of the image. For each k apply (TL) with U := ℝ^P to (A, B) := (E ∩ Σ_k, Σ_k) and to (A, B) := (E ∩ Σ_k, E): these are Borel, and Hⁿ(Σ_k), Hⁿ(E) < ∞. So for Hⁿ-a.e. w ∈ E ∩ Σ_k, the sets E, E ∩ Σ_k and Σ_k have the same approximate tangent spaces at w. Let Bad_E be the union of these countably many null exceptional sets, of ℝ^P ∖ E₁, and of f(M' ∖ good), which is Hⁿ-null as f is Lipschitz. For w ∈ E ∖ Bad_E, every x ∈ f⁻¹(w) ∩ M' is good; if x ∈ K_m and k := k(m), then w ∈ E ∩ Σ_k, Σ_k has approximate tangent space Df(x)(T_xM) at w (good), and hence so does E. By uniqueness, Π_w := T_wE exists and Df(x)(T_xM) = Π_w for every x ∈ f⁻¹(w) ∩ M'.
7. Integer multiplicity in the fibres (Simon 3.7–3.8). Let w ∈ E ∖ Bad_E and fix a unit orientation ζ_w of Π_w. For x ∈ f⁻¹(w) ∩ M', ζ̂(x) is a unit orientation of Df(x)(T_xM) = Π_w (5(a), 6), so ζ̂(x) = ε(x)ζ_w with ε(x) ∈ {1, −1} (L3). Hence V(w) = m(w)ζ_w with m(w) := Σ_{x∈f⁻¹(w)∩M'} ε(x)θ(x) ∈ ℤ (a finite sum, w ∈ E₁) and |m(w)| ≤ Σ_{x∈f⁻¹(w)∩M'} θ(x).
8. Borel versions; restriction to positive multiplicity. ν(w) := |V(w)| is Borel and ν = |m| on E ∖ Bad_E (7 and (L2)). Define the Borel function N'(w) := ⌊ν(w) + 1/2⌋ ∈ ℕ (so N' = |m| on E ∖ Bad_E), the Borel map ζ'(w) := V(w)/ν(w) if ν(w) > 0 and ζ'(w) := 0 otherwise, and the Borel carrier C := {w ∈ E : N'(w) ≥ 1}. For w ∈ C ∖ Bad_E: m(w) ≠ 0, ζ'(w) = sgn(m(w))ζ_w is a unit orientation of Π_w, and N'(w)ζ'(w) = m(w)ζ_w = V(w). For w ∈ E ∖ (C ∪ Bad_E): m(w) = 0, so V(w) = 0. For w ∉ E, V(w) = 0 (empty fibre). Hence V = 1_C·N'·ζ' Hⁿ-a.e. This removes from the carrier the points where Simon's multiplicity |m| vanishes.
9. R' := (C, N', ζ') is an IMRep in U representing Q.
 - measurableSet_carrier: C is Borel.
 - carrier_subset: C ⊆ E ⊆ f(K) ⊆ U.
 - rectifiable: C ⊆ E is countably n-rectifiable by 3(c).
 - measurable_mult: N' is Borel. mult_pos: N' ≥ 1 on C by definition of C.
 - locallyIntegrable_mult: for compact K₀ ⊆ U, ∫_{C∩K₀} N' dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{E∖Bad_E} |m| dHⁿ ≤ ∫ Σ_{x∈f⁻¹(w)∩M'} θ(x) dHⁿ(w) < ∞ (7 and 4).
 - aestronglyMeasurable_orient: ζ' is Borel with values in the finite-dimensional Λ_n, hence strongly measurable.
 - orients: (TL) with U := ℝ^P and (A, B) := (C, E) (C ⊆ E Borel, Hⁿ(E) < ∞) shows that for Hⁿ-a.e. w ∈ C, C and E have the same approximate tangent spaces at w. For such w ∉ Bad_E, T_wE = Π_w exists, so HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C w Π_w, and ζ'(w) is a unit orientation of Π_w (8). So the orientation field holds Hⁿ⌞C-a.e.
 - Represents: for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), w ↦ N'(w)ζ'(w)(ω(w)) is integrable on C (bounded by N'·sup|ω|_E via (L2), and N' is integrable on C ∩ tsupport ω). By 8 and (B): R'.action ω = ∫_C N'(w)ζ'(w)(ω(w)) dHⁿ(w) = ∫ V(w)(ω(w)) dHⁿ(w) = Q(ω).
 Hence Q is integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity Q). (If n > P then Hⁿ = 0 on ℝ^P, every set above is null, C = ∅, and the same construction gives Q = 0 = τ(∅, 0, 0).) ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to M = M_R ∩ K and, by a cutoff, to a globally C¹ Lipschitz f; fix a Borel orientation ξ̃, the Jacobian J = |Df_#ξ̃| ≤ Λⁿ and M₊ = {J > 0}; (TL) shows a.e. point of M is oriented.

Bi-Lipschitz pieces of M (built from Lipschitz parametrizations, SimonGMT areaRegularSet and Mathlib's partition lemma) and the partition lemma for g = f∘F_i give countably many disjoint Borel pieces A_k covering M₊ a.e. with f injective on each; Lemma T gives the tangent planes of M and of f(A_k) along the pieces.
On disjoint compact K_m ⊆ A_k the area formula and J_{f∘F} = J_F·J give ∫_{M'}hJ = ∫ Σ_{x∈f⁻¹(w)∩M'} h(x) dHⁿ(w); hence Q(ω) = ∫ V(w)(ω(w)) dHⁿ with V(w) = Σ_{fibre} θζ̂.
(TL) identifies T_wE with Df(x)(T_xM) for every x in the fibre, so V(w) = m(w)ζ_w with m(w) ∈ ℤ (Simon 3.7–3.8).

Borel versions N' = ⌊|V| + 1/2⌋, ζ' = V/|V| on C = {w ∈ E : N'(w) ≥ 1} (positive multiplicity, correcting Simon 3.9) form an IMRep in U; (TL) on C ⊆ E gives the orientation field and (B) gives Q = τ(C, N', ζ').

If ∂X = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes X; vacuous for n = 0), then ∂Q = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes Q). This is Simon Ch. 6, 2.24(1) for the push-forward Q = f_#X.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5(d) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 2.24(1), ∂f_#T = f_#∂T, chapter-06.txt lines 413–415), specialized to a compact set K, an open O ⊇ K and a general f. The mollification is performed on a compactly supported perturbation of the identity, so that every pulled-back form is a test form in U.
Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; μ := Hⁿ⌞M. For a C¹ map ψ and a p-form α put ψ^#α(x) := α(ψ(x))∘Dψ(x) = (α (ψ x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ ψ x).
0. Reduction. If n = 0, BoundaryVanishes Q holds by definition. Let n = m + 1. BoundaryVanishes Q means Q.boundary = 0, i.e. Q(dη) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟^m(U), where dη := exteriorDerivative η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (Simon 6.2.3; SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply). Likewise the hypothesis BoundaryVanishes X gives X(dη') = 0 for every η' ∈ 𝒟^m(U). Fix η ∈ 𝒟^m(U).
1. Cutoff. V₀ := O ∩ U is open and contains K. Choose χ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, compact support K₁ := tsupport χ ⊆ V₀, and χ = 1 on an open set W₀ ⊇ K (smooth Urysohn lemma for the compact K inside the open V₀; e.g. Mathlib ContDiffBump functions on a finite cover of K). Define φ(x) := χ(x)·f(x) + (1 − χ(x))·x.
2. Properties of φ. (a) φ is C¹ on ℝ^P: on the open set O both χ and f are C¹; on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K₁ we have χ = 0 identically, so φ = id there; and O ∪ (ℝ^P ∖ K₁) = ℝ^P because K₁ ⊆ O. (b) φ(x) = x for x ∉ K₁, and K₁ is a compact subset of U. (c) φ = f on the open set W₀ ⊇ K, so φ(x) = f(x) and Dφ(x) = Df(x) for every x ∈ K (the derivative depends only on the germ; Mathlib Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
3. Smooth approximation. There are C^∞ maps ψ_k : ℝ^P → ℝ^P (k ∈ ℕ), a compact K' ⊆ U and C ≥ 0 with ψ_k(x) = x for x ∉ K', ‖Dψ_k(x)‖ ≤ C for all k and x, and ψ_k(x) → φ(x), Dψ_k(x) → Dφ(x) for every x. Proof: g := φ − id is C¹ with tsupport g ⊆ K₁. Choose δ > 0 with K' := {x : dist(x, K₁) ≤ δ} ⊆ U (K₁ compact, U open). Let ρ_k ≥ 0 be smooth mollifiers with ∫ρ_k = 1 and support in B_{δ/(k+1)}(0), and put ψ_k := id + ρ_k * g. Then ρ_k * g is C^∞ with support in K', ρ_k * g → g and D(ρ_k * g) = ρ_k * Dg → Dg uniformly (g and Dg are uniformly continuous, having compact support), and ‖Dψ_k‖ ≤ 1 + sup‖Dg‖ =: C. (This is the accepted DAG declaration dpf_smooth_approx_compact_perturbation.)
4. Pulled-back test forms. Let α be a test p-form in U and ψ := ψ_k. Then ψ^#α is C^∞ (chain rule) and vanishes on the open set ℝ^P ∖ (K' ∪ tsupport α): near such x, ψ = id, so ψ^#α = α = 0 near x. Hence tsupport ψ^#α ⊆ K' ∪ tsupport α, a compact subset of U, and ψ^#α ∈ 𝒟^p(U). (Accepted DAG declaration dpf_pb_smooth_pullback_isTestForm.)
5. Naturality. For the C^∞ map ψ_k and the smooth form η, d(ψ_k^#η) = ψ_k^#(dη) pointwise (Simon 6.1.14; Mathlib extDeriv_pullback, applicable because ψ_k is C² and η is differentiable).
6. Vanishing along the approximation. By step 4, ψ_k^#η ∈ 𝒟^m(U), so ∂X = 0 and step 5 give 0 = X(d(ψ_k^#η)) = X(ψ_k^#(dη)). Since ψ_k^#(dη) ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (step 4 with α = dη) and R represents X: 0 = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)((dη)(ψ_k(x))∘Dψ_k(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every k.
7. Passage to the limit. Put α := dη, a continuous n-form with compact support in U, and K'' := K' ∪ tsupport α, a compact subset of U. For every k the integrand of step 6 vanishes off K'': if x ∉ K' then ψ_k(x) = x, and α(x) = 0 when x ∉ tsupport α. For μ-a.e. x, ξ(x) is a unit orientation (R.orients), so |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ (operator norm). Hence the integrands are bounded by θ(x)·1_{K''}(x)·‖α‖_∞·Cⁿ (‖β∘L‖ ≤ ‖β‖‖L‖ⁿ), which is μ-integrable by R.locallyIntegrable_mult. Pointwise, α(ψ_k(x))∘Dψ_k(x) → α(φ(x))∘Dφ(x), by continuity of α and of (β, L) ↦ β∘L. Dominated convergence yields ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(α(φ(x))∘Dφ(x)) dHⁿ(x) = lim_k 0 = 0. (This is the accepted DAG declaration dpf_pb_imrep_pullback_integral_tendsto.)
8. Conclusion. By step 2(c), α(φ(x))∘Dφ(x) = α(f(x))∘Df(x) for every x ∈ K, hence for μ-a.e. x (Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0). Therefore Q(dη) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(α(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(α(φ(x))∘Dφ(x)) dHⁿ(x) = 0. As η ∈ 𝒟^m(U) was arbitrary, Q.boundary = 0, i.e. BoundaryVanishes Q. ∎

Mollify φ − id to smooth ψ_k = id off a compact K' ⊆ U with uniformly bounded derivatives and ψ_k → φ, Dψ_k → Dφ pointwise.
ψ_k^#η is a test form in U and d(ψ_k^#η) = ψ_k^#(dη) (Mathlib extDeriv_pullback), so ∂X = 0 gives ∫_M θξ(dη(ψ_k)∘Dψ_k) = 0.
Dominated convergence on the fixed compact K' ∪ spt dη gives ∫_M θξ(dη(φ)∘Dφ) = 0, i.e. Q(dη) = 0.

subproblems.title: Unit orientations under linear pull-back: the Hadamard bound and the fixed-plane identity
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Q ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace, ξ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n) a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q: ξ(α) = ±α(τ₁, …, τₙ) for all n-covectors α, for an orthonormal family τ spanning Q), and L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P a continuous linear map. Then: (a) |ξ(α∘L)| ≤ |α|_E·‖L‖ⁿ for every n-covector α, where α∘L := α.compContinuousLinearMap L, |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α is the Euclidean coefficient norm (Simon 6.1.15) and ‖L‖ is the operator norm; (b) if Lv = v for every v ∈ Q, then ξ(α∘L) = ξ(α) for every n-covector α.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ξ : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (L : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ (α.compContinuousLinearMap L)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α * ‖L‖ ^ n) ∧ ((∀ v ∈ Q, L v = v) → ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ξ (α.compContinuousLinearMap L) = ξ α)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: facts (L1) and (L4) and steps 4 and 7(d) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 1.1–1.7 and 3.4: ⟨α∘L, τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ⟩ = ⟨α, Lτ₁∧⋯∧Lτₙ⟩, and the Hadamard bound for |Lτ₁∧⋯∧Lτₙ|).
Notation. |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α (Euclidean coefficient norm, Simon 6.1.15); ‖L‖ the operator norm; α∘L := α.compContinuousLinearMap L, so (α∘L)(w₁, …, wₙ) = α(Lw₁, …, Lwₙ).
0. Set-up. By IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q there are an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) with span τ = Q and s ∈ {1, −1} such that ξ(β) = s·β(τ) for every n-covector β. For every n-covector α, (α∘L)(τ) = α(Lτ₁, …, Lτₙ), so ξ(α∘L) = s·α(v) with v := (Lτ₁, …, Lτₙ).
Part (a).
1. Dependent case. If v is linearly dependent, then α(v) = 0 because α is alternating (Mathlib AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent applied to the underlying alternating map of α). So |ξ(α∘L)| = 0 ≤ |α|_E·‖L‖ⁿ, as both factors are ≥ 0.
2. Gram bound. Let v be linearly independent. By the accepted sibling covectorEuclideanNorm_gram_bounds, part (1) (Cauchy–Schwarz and Cauchy–Binet), |α(v)| ≤ |α|_E·(det G)^{1/2}, where G := (⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j}.
3. Hadamard. By the accepted sibling dpf_exists_orthonormal_frame_det_gram (Gram–Schmidt) there is an orthonormal family σ with span σ = span v such that, for A := (⟨σ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j}, det G = (det A)² and |det A| ≤ Π_i |v_i|. Hence (det G)^{1/2} = |det A| ≤ Π_i |v_i|.
4. Conclusion of (a). |v_i| = |Lτ_i| ≤ ‖L‖·|τ_i| = ‖L‖ for each i, so Π_i |v_i| ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ. By steps 2–3, |ξ(α∘L)| = |α(v)| ≤ |α|_E·‖L‖ⁿ. (For n = 0 the family v is empty and linearly independent, G is the empty matrix with det G = 1, the empty product is 1, and the bound reads |α()| ≤ |α|_E.)
Part (b).
5. Assume Lw = w for every w ∈ Q. Each τ_i lies in span τ = Q, so Lτ_i = τ_i and v = τ. Hence ξ(α∘L) = s·α(τ) = ξ(α) for every n-covector α. ∎
proof_key_steps: ξ(α∘L) = ±α(Lτ₁, …, Lτₙ) for the orthonormal frame τ of Q.
If (Lτ_i) is dependent the value is 0; otherwise Cauchy–Binet gives |α(Lτ)| ≤ |α|_E det(⟨Lτ_i, Lτ_j⟩)^{1/2}.
Gram–Schmidt (Hadamard) gives det(⟨Lτ_i, Lτ_j⟩)^{1/2} ≤ Π|Lτ_i| ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ, proving (a).
If L fixes Q pointwise then Lτ = τ, so ξ(α∘L) = ξ(α), proving (b).

subproblems.title: A map fixing N to first order fixes the orientation of an integer multiplicity triple carried by N
subproblems.statement: Let P, n, d ∈ ℕ, N ⊆ ℝ^P an embedded C¹ d-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d N), O ⊆ ℝ^P a Borel set, U ⊆ ℝ^P, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) with Hⁿ(M ∖ N) = 0 (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P such that f(x) = x and Df(x)v = v for every x ∈ N ∩ O and every v ∈ T_xN (tangentSpace N x; Df(x) = fderiv ℝ f x). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ O (i.e. Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ O)-a.e.): f(x) = x and ξ(x)(α∘Df(x)) = ξ(x)(α) for every n-covector α (α∘L = α.compContinuousLinearMap L).

Source: steps 3–4 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 3, §1 and Ch. 2, §4: approximate tangent planes of a set carried by N lie in TₓN; a retraction fixing N to first order fixes the carried orientation).
Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; μ := Hⁿ⌞M (M = R.carrier is Borel); Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x.
1. Almost every point of M lies in N. Since M is Borel, μ(ℝ^P ∖ N) = Hⁿ((ℝ^P ∖ N) ∩ M) = Hⁿ(M ∖ N) = 0 (Mathlib Measure.restrict_apply' for the measurable restricting set M). So x ∈ N for μ-a.e. x.
2. Orientations. By the field R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there is a linear subspace Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q_x.
3. Tangent inclusion. Let x satisfy steps 1 and 2. The accepted sibling approxTangent_le_submanifold_tangentSpace applies to N (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d N), x ∈ N, Hⁿ(M ∖ N) = 0 and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x, and gives Q_x ⊆ tangentSpace N x.
4. Fixed orientation. If moreover x ∈ O, then x ∈ N ∩ O, so f(x) = x by hypothesis. For every w ∈ Q_x we have w ∈ tangentSpace N x by step 3, so Df(x)w = w by hypothesis. The sibling dor_lmb_pc_unitOrientation_comp, part (b), applied to ξ(x), Q_x and L := Df(x), gives ξ(x)(α∘Df(x)) = ξ(x)(α) for every n-covector α.
5. Restriction. The properties of steps 1–2 hold μ-a.e., hence Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ O)-a.e. (restriction of the measure to the subset M ∩ O ⊆ M; Mathlib ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset). Since M ∩ O is Borel, x ∈ M ∩ O, and in particular x ∈ O, for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ O)-a.e. x (Mathlib ae_restrict_mem). By steps 3–4, for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ O)-a.e. x we have f(x) = x and ξ(x)(α∘Df(x)) = ξ(x)(α) for every n-covector α. ∎
proof_key_steps: Hⁿ(M ∖ N) = 0 and R.orients: a.e. x ∈ M lies in N and ξ(x) is a unit orientation of an approximate tangent plane Q_x of M.
approxTangent_le_submanifold_tangentSpace gives Q_x ⊆ T_xN.
For x ∈ N ∩ O, f(x) = x and Df(x) fixes T_xN ⊇ Q_x, so part (b) of dor_lmb_pc_unitOrientation_comp gives ξ(x)(α∘Df(x)) = ξ(x)(α).
Restrict the a.e. statements from Hⁿ⌞M to Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ O).

subproblems.title: Mass bound for the competitor Z + f_#X when f fixes Z on G and Y = Z + X
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, G ⊆ ℝ^P open with G ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContained G U: closure G is compact and contained in U), O ⊆ ℝ^P open with G ⊆ O, f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on O, and Λ ≥ 0 with ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ Λ for every x ∈ G (Df(x) = fderiv ℝ f x, operator norm). Let RZ = (M_Z, θ_Z, ξ_Z), RX = (M_X, θ_X, ξ_X) and RY = (M_Y, θ_Y, ξ_Y) be integer multiplicity triples in U (IMRep U n) and Y, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and write τ(R)(ω) := R.action ω = ∫_{M_R} θ_R ξ_R(ω) dHⁿ (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Assume: RY represents Y; Y(ω) = τ(RZ)(ω) + τ(RX)(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_Z ∩ G (i.e. Hⁿ⌞(M_Z ∩ G)-a.e.), f(x) = x and ξ_Z(x)(α∘Df(x)) = ξ_Z(x)(α) for every n-covector α; Hⁿ(M_X ∖ G) = 0; and S(ω) = τ(RZ)(ω) + ∫_{M_X} θ_X(x)·ξ_X(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Then M_G(S) ≤ Λⁿ·μ_{RY}(G), i.e. S.massOn G ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(Λⁿ)·RY.measure G, where M_G(S) is the supremum of S(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ G and |ω(z)|_E ≤ 1 for all z (Simon 6.2.5, Euclidean coefficient norm) and μ_{RY} = θ_Y·Hⁿ⌞M_Y.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U G O : Set (Euclid P)) (RZ RX RY : IMRep U n) (Y S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P) (Λ : ℝ), IsOpen U → IsOpen G → CompactlyContained G U → IsOpen O → G ⊆ O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → 0 ≤ Λ → (∀ x ∈ G, ‖fderiv ℝ f x‖ ≤ Λ) → RY.Represents Y → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Y ω = RZ.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) + RX.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (RZ.carrier ∩ G)), f x = x ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, RZ.orient x (α.compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) = RZ.orient x α) → μHE[n] (RX.carrier \ G) = 0 → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, S ω = RZ.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) + ∫ x in RX.carrier, (RX.mult x : ℝ) * RX.orient x (((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∂μHE[n]) → S.massOn G ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (Λ ^ n) * RY.measure G
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof, i.e. the competitor mass bound in Simon's proof of 7.2.4, (8)–(9) (chapter-07.txt lines 222–246), for the competitor S = Z + f_#X with f fixing Z on G. The vector-measure identity of the parent's step 7(c) is obtained from three accepted DAG declarations.
Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]. For an IMRep R = (M_R, θ_R, ξ_R) put ν_R(x) := 1_{M_R}(x)·θ_R(x)·ξ_R(x) ∈ Λ_n (MultiVector P n), τ(R)(ω) := R.action ω = ∫_{M_R} θ_R ξ_R(ω) dHⁿ, and μ_R := R.measure = θ_R·Hⁿ⌞M_R. Write RZ = (M_Z, θ_Z, ξ_Z), RX = (M_X, θ_X, ξ_X), RY = (M_Y, θ_Y, ξ_Y). Ḡ := closure G is a compact subset of U (CompactlyContained G U). Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x; ‖·‖ operator norms; |·|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm.
1. Vector density identity. (a) The accepted sibling rsdic_exists_imrep_int_combination (U open, p₁ = p₂ = 1) gives an IMRep R in U with ν_R = ν_{RZ} + ν_{RX} Hⁿ-a.e. on ℝ^P. (b) The accepted sibling rsdic_imrep_action_int_combination turns (a) into R.action ω = τ(RZ)(ω) + τ(RX)(ω) = Y(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); thus R represents Y. (c) RY also represents Y, so the accepted sibling imrep_weighted_orient_indicator_ae_eq gives ν_R = ν_{RY} Hⁿ-a.e. on M_R ∪ M_Y. (d) Outside M_R ∪ M_Y both ν_R and ν_{RY} vanish. Combining (a), (c) and (d): ν_{RY} = ν_{RZ} + ν_{RX} Hⁿ-a.e. on ℝ^P.
2. An admissible form and its pull-back. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) be admissible for S.massOn G: tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(z)|_E ≤ 1 for all z. Put φ(x) := ω(f(x))∘Df(x) for x ∈ G and φ(x) := 0 for x ∉ G. As f and Df are continuous on the open set O ⊇ G (f is C¹ on O), φ is continuous on the open set G, hence Borel on ℝ^P. Moreover ‖φ(x)‖ ≤ ‖ω‖_∞·Λⁿ for all x (‖β∘L‖ ≤ ‖β‖‖L‖ⁿ, ‖Df‖ ≤ Λ on G), and φ = 0 off G ⊆ Ḡ.
3. Integrability. For R ∈ {RZ, RX, RY}: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_R, ξ_R(x) is a unit orientation (R.orients), so |ξ_R(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖. Hence x ↦ ν_R(x)(φ(x)) is a.e.-strongly measurable, vanishes off M_R ∩ Ḡ, and is bounded by ‖ω‖_∞Λⁿ·θ_R(x)·1_{M_R∩Ḡ}(x); since ∫_{M_R∩Ḡ} θ_R dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult), it is Hⁿ-integrable. In the same way x ↦ θ_Z(x)ξ_Z(x)(ω(x)) is integrable on M_Z (tsupport ω ⊆ Ḡ), and x ↦ θ_X(x)ξ_X(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) is integrable on M_X, as it agrees Hⁿ⌞M_X-a.e. with ν_{RX}(φ) (step 5).
4. The Z part. τ(RZ)(ω) = ∫ ν_{RZ}(φ) dHⁿ. Indeed, for x ∈ M_Z ∖ G we have x ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 = φ(x). M_Z ∩ G is Borel, so the hypothesis on Hⁿ⌞(M_Z ∩ G) says: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_Z ∩ G, f(x) = x and ξ_Z(x)(α∘Df(x)) = ξ_Z(x)(α) for all α. For such x, φ(x) = ω(x)∘Df(x), and with α := ω(x), ξ_Z(x)(φ(x)) = ξ_Z(x)(ω(x)). So the integrands of τ(RZ)(ω) = ∫_{M_Z} θ_Zξ_Z(ω) dHⁿ and ∫ ν_{RZ}(φ) dHⁿ agree Hⁿ-a.e.
5. The X part. ∫_{M_X} θ_X(x)ξ_X(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x) = ∫ ν_{RX}(φ) dHⁿ, since the integrands agree on M_X ∩ G and Hⁿ(M_X ∖ G) = 0.
6. The Y part. By the hypothesis on S, steps 4–5, linearity of the integral (step 3) and step 1: S(ω) = ∫ (ν_{RZ} + ν_{RX})(x)(φ(x)) dHⁿ(x) = ∫ ν_{RY}(x)(φ(x)) dHⁿ(x) = ∫_{M_Y∩G} θ_Y(x)·ξ_Y(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x).
7. Pointwise bound. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_Y, ξ_Y(x) is a unit orientation of some n-plane. For such x ∈ G, the sibling dor_lmb_pc_unitOrientation_comp, part (a), with α := ω(f(x)) and L := Df(x), gives |ξ_Y(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x))| ≤ |ω(f(x))|_E·‖Df(x)‖ⁿ ≤ 1·Λⁿ.
8. Conclusion. By steps 6–7, S(ω) ≤ Λⁿ∫_{M_Y∩G} θ_Y dHⁿ = Λⁿ·(μ_{RY}(G)).toReal, where μ_{RY}(G) ≤ μ_{RY}(Ḡ) < ∞. Hence ofReal(S(ω)) ≤ ofReal(Λⁿ)·μ_{RY}(G) (Λ ≥ 0). S.massOn G is the supremum of ofReal(S(ω)) over the admissible ω (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.massOn), so S.massOn G ≤ ofReal(Λⁿ)·RY.measure G. ∎
proof_key_steps: Three accepted lemmas give the vector-density identity 1_{M_Y}θ_Yξ_Y = 1_{M_Z}θ_Zξ_Z + 1_{M_X}θ_Xξ_X Hⁿ-a.e.
For admissible ω, the bounded Borel form φ = 1_G·ω(f)∘Df represents both parts: f fixes Z a.e. on M_Z ∩ G, and M_X ⊆ G a.e.
Hence S(ω) = ∫_{M_Y∩G} θ_Yξ_Y(ω(f)∘Df) dHⁿ, all integrands being dominated on the compact closure of G.

Accepted proof:
Source: Simon 6.1 (Λ^n with the inner product making e^{i_1}∧⋯∧e^{i_n} orthonormal, 6.1.15) and 6.3.4–3.5 (|v_1∧⋯∧v_n| = J); these are the algebraic facts behind "M_W(τ(M,θ,ξ)) = ∫_{M∩W}θ dH^n" (6.3.2(3)) and the Jacobian bound in step 5 of the parent proof.
1. Notation. 𝓘 := the strictly increasing maps I : Fin n → Fin P; e_k := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ k; for I ∈ 𝓘, α_I := α(e_{I 1}, …, e_{I n}); by definition |α|_E = (Σ_{I∈𝓘} α_I²)^{1/2} (the sum over all I with the StrictMono filter). For v = (v_1, …, v_n) let V be the P×n matrix V_{k,j} := ⟨e_k, v_j⟩ = v_j(k), and for I ∈ 𝓘 let V_I be the n×n matrix (V_I)_{a,j} := v_j(I a).
2. Expansion. α(v) = Σ_{I∈𝓘} α_I·det V_I. Proof: write v_j = Σ_k v_j(k)e_k and expand by multilinearity: α(v) = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_j v_j(f j))·α(e_{f 1}, …, e_{f n}). Terms with f not injective vanish (α alternating, repeated argument). Each injective f is uniquely f = I∘σ with I ∈ 𝓘 (the increasing enumeration of its range) and σ a permutation, and α(e_{I∘σ}) = sgn(σ)α_I. So α(v) = Σ_I α_I Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j v_j(I(σ j)) = Σ_I α_I det V_I by the Leibniz formula.
3. Cauchy–Binet. Σ_{I∈𝓘} (det V_I)² = det(VᵀV) = det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j}. Proof: det(VᵀV) = Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i (Σ_k V_{k,i}V_{k,σ i}) = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_i V_{f i, i})·Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i V_{f i, σ i} = Σ_f (Π_i V_{f i, i})·det(V_f), where V_f is the n×n matrix (V_{f a, j})_{a,j}. det V_f = 0 unless f is injective, and for f = I∘σ, det V_f = sgn(σ) det V_I (row permutation). Hence det(VᵀV) = Σ_I det V_I·Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i V_{I(σ i), i} = Σ_I (det V_I)² (Leibniz formula again).
4. Part (1). By step 2 and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in ℝ^𝓘, |α(v)| ≤ (Σ_I α_I²)^{1/2}(Σ_I (det V_I)²)^{1/2} = |α|_E·(det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩))^{1/2} by step 3 (the Gram determinant is ≥ 0, being a sum of squares).
5. Part (2). For n = 0 take α the constant 0-covector with value 1: |α|_E = 1 (𝓘 consists of the empty map) and α() = 1. For n ≥ 1 let α(u_1, …, u_n) := det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b}; it is multilinear, alternating and continuous, hence an n-covector, and α(τ) = det(⟨τ_a, τ_b⟩) = det I = 1. Moreover α_I = det(⟨τ_a, e_{I b}⟩)_{a,b} = det(T_I) with T the P×n matrix of τ (transposes have equal determinants), so by step 3 applied to v = τ: |α|_E² = Σ_I det(T_I)² = det(⟨τ_a, τ_b⟩) = 1. Hence |α|_E = 1 ≤ 1.
6. Degenerate cases are covered: if n > P then 𝓘 = ∅, |α|_E = 0, every n-covector vanishes (n vectors in ℝ^P are dependent) and there is no orthonormal n-family.
proof_key_steps: Expansion α(v) = Σ_I α(e_I) det V_I by multilinearity and alternation.
Cauchy–Binet: Σ_I (det V_I)² = det(v_i·v_j).
Cauchy–Schwarz gives (1); the covector u ↦ det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩) gives (2).

subproblems.title: Gram–Schmidt frame: det G(v) = (det A)², det A ≠ 0, |det A| ≤ ∏|v_a|
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let v = (v_1, …, v_n) (indexed by Fin n) be a linearly independent family in ℝ^P (Euclid P). Then there is an orthonormal family σ = (σ_1, …, σ_n) in ℝ^P with span{σ_1, …, σ_n} = span{v_1, …, v_n} such that, for the n×n real matrix A with entries A_{ab} := ⟨σ_a, v_b⟩: (i) det(⟨v_a, v_b⟩)_{a,b} = (det A)²; (ii) det A ≠ 0; (iii) |det A| ≤ ∏_a |v_a|. Here ⟨·,·⟩ and |·| are the Euclidean inner product and norm.

Accepted proof:
Source: steps 3–5 of the parent proof (Gram–Schmidt, G = AᵀA, and the upper-triangular determinant bound), with the details filled in. This is Simon 6.3.4–3.5's expansion in an orthonormal basis of the image space, with the basis chosen by Gram–Schmidt.

Notation: ⟨·,·⟩ and |·| are the Euclidean inner product and norm of ℝ^P.

1. The subspace W.
   - Let W := span{v_1, …, v_n} ⊆ ℝ^P with the restricted inner product, a finite-dimensional inner product space. Let ι_W : W → ℝ^P be the inclusion.
   - Since v is linearly independent, dim W = n = card(Fin n) (finrank_span_eq_card).
   - Each v_b lies in W. Let w_b ∈ W be v_b regarded as an element of W, so ι_W(w_b) = v_b.
   - w is linearly independent in W, because ι_W ∘ w = v is linearly independent (LinearIndependent.of_comp).
   - w spans W. The map ι_W sends span(w) onto span(ι_W ∘ w) = span v = W = ι_W(W) (Submodule.map_span, Set.range_comp, Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype). The induced map on submodules is injective (Submodule.map_injective_of_injective), so span(w) = W, the top submodule of W.

2. Gram–Schmidt. Apply Gram–Schmidt orthonormalisation in W to w, in the order of Fin n (Mathlib InnerProductSpace.gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis, with the hypothesis finrank W = card(Fin n) from step 1).
   - This yields an orthonormal basis b = (b_1, …, b_n) of W.
   - Its coefficient matrix for w is upper triangular: ⟨b_a, w_c⟩ = 0 whenever c < a (gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis_inv_triangular).
   - Consequently the basis determinant of the family w with respect to b is the product of the diagonal entries: det_b(w) = ∏_a ⟨b_a, w_a⟩ (gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis_det; det_b is Module.Basis.det of b.toBasis).

3. The frame σ. Define σ_a := ι_W(b_a) ∈ ℝ^P.
   - Norms and inner products of elements of W are computed in ℝ^P, so |σ_a| = 1 and ⟨σ_a, σ_c⟩ = 0 for a ≠ c. Hence σ is orthonormal.
   - b is a basis, so span b = W. Therefore span σ = span(ι_W ∘ b) = ι_W(span b) = ι_W(W) = W = span v (Set.range_comp, Submodule.map_span, Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype).

4. The coefficient matrix.
   - For an orthonormal basis, the a-th coordinate of w_c is ⟨b_a, w_c⟩ (OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis_repr_apply, OrthonormalBasis.repr_apply_apply).
   - Inner products in W are those of ℝ^P, so ⟨b_a, w_c⟩ = ⟨σ_a, v_c⟩ = A_{ac}. Thus A is the matrix of the family w in the basis b (Module.Basis.toMatrix_apply).
   - Hence det A = det_b(w) (Module.Basis.det_apply) = ∏_a ⟨σ_a, v_a⟩ by step 2.

5. (i) Gram identity.
   - Fix a and c. Parseval's identity for the orthonormal basis b of W (OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner) gives ⟨v_a, v_c⟩ = ⟨w_a, w_c⟩ = Σ_k ⟨w_a, b_k⟩⟨b_k, w_c⟩.
   - By symmetry of the real inner product (real_inner_comm), Σ_k ⟨w_a, b_k⟩⟨b_k, w_c⟩ = Σ_k ⟨σ_k, v_a⟩⟨σ_k, v_c⟩ = Σ_k A_{ka} A_{kc} = (AᵀA)_{ac}.
   - So (⟨v_a, v_c⟩)_{a,c} = AᵀA, and det(⟨v_a, v_c⟩) = det(Aᵀ)·det(A) = (det A)² (Matrix.det_mul, Matrix.det_transpose).

6. (ii) det A ≠ 0. By step 4, det A = det_b(w). By step 1, w is linearly independent and spans W, so det_b(w) is a unit (Module.Basis.is_basis_iff_det), hence nonzero.

7. (iii) The bound.
   - By step 4 and multiplicativity of the absolute value (Finset.abs_prod), |det A| = ∏_a |⟨σ_a, v_a⟩|.
   - For each a, Cauchy–Schwarz and |σ_a| = 1 give |⟨σ_a, v_a⟩| ≤ |σ_a|·|v_a| = |v_a| (abs_real_inner_le_norm).
   - All factors are nonnegative, so the products compare factor by factor (Finset.prod_le_prod₀): |det A| ≤ ∏_a |v_a|.

8. The case n = 0 is covered by steps 1–7, which never assume n > 0. All families are empty, W = {0}, A is the empty matrix with det A = 1 ≠ 0, det(⟨v_a, v_b⟩) = 1 = 1², and the empty product is 1. ∎

Formalization notes (everything cited, including gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis and gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis_det, is available after import GMT.Ch07.Submission):
- Take W := Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v), w j := ⟨v j, Submodule.subset_span ⟨j, rfl⟩⟩ and b := InnerProductSpace.gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis (finrank_span_eq_card hv) w. Use fun i => (b i : Euclid P) as σ.
- Mathlib's GramMatrix and NormDet files are not imported. So prove the Gram identity entrywise with Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.transpose_apply and b.sum_inner_mul_inner (w i) (w j), after simp only [Submodule.coe_inner] and real_inner_comm.
- For (ii), use (Module.Basis.is_basis_iff_det b.toBasis).mp ⟨hw, hspan_w⟩, not basisOfLinearIndependentOfCardEqFinrank, which needs a Nonempty index.
- For (iii), use Finset.prod_le_prod₀. Plain Finset.prod_le_prod needs MulLeftMono and fails for ℝ.

Gram–Schmidt in W gives an orthonormal basis b with det_b(w) = ∏⟨b_a, w_a⟩ (upper-triangular coefficients).
σ := b regarded in ℝ^P is orthonormal, with span σ = W = span v.
A_{ac} = ⟨σ_a, v_c⟩ is the coefficient matrix of w in b, so det A = det_b(w) = ∏⟨σ_a, v_a⟩.
Parseval gives G(v) = AᵀA, hence det G(v) = (det A)².
det A = det_b(w) is a unit because w is a basis of W, so det A ≠ 0.
|det A| = ∏|⟨σ_a, v_a⟩| ≤ ∏|v_a| by Cauchy–Schwarz and |σ_a| = 1.

Notation: μ := μHE[n]; M_i := R_i.carrier, θ_i := R_i.mult, ξ_i := R_i.orient; A := M₁ ∪ M₂, a Borel subset of U; sgn : ℤ → {−1, 0, 1} is the sign; for an integer c, |c| ∈ ℕ is its absolute value. 1. Borel orientations. ξ_i is AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞M_i, so there is a strongly measurable (Borel) ξ̃_i : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) with ξ̃_i = ξ_i μ⌞M_i-a.e. (Mathlib AEStronglyMeasurable.mk / ae_eq_mk). Equivalently: for μ-a.e. x, x ∈ M_i ⇒ ξ̃_i(x) = ξ_i(x).

2. Borel sign on the overlap. Define σ(x) := 1 if ξ̃₂(x) = ξ̃₁(x) and σ(x) := −1 otherwise. The set {ξ̃₂ = ξ̃₁} is Borel (both maps are strongly measurable into the metrizable space Λ_n(ℝ^P)), so σ : ℝ^P → ℤ is Borel. Claim: for μ-a.e. x, x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ ⇒ ξ̃₂(x) = σ(x)ξ̃₁(x). Indeed, by the sibling lemma overlap_orientation_sign and step 1, for μ⌞(M₁ ∩ M₂)-a.e. x we have ξ̃₁(x) = ξ₁(x), ξ̃₂(x) = ξ₂(x) and ξ₂(x) = ±ξ₁(x), hence ξ̃₂(x) = ξ̃₁(x) or ξ̃₂(x) = −ξ̃₁(x). In the first case σ(x) = 1; in the second case, if ξ̃₂(x) ≠ ξ̃₁(x) then σ(x) = −1 and ξ̃₂(x) = −ξ̃₁(x), while if ξ̃₂(x) = ξ̃₁(x) we are in the first case. In all cases ξ̃₂(x) = σ(x)ξ̃₁(x). (This equality test replaces the parent proof's coordinate test Σ_I⟨e^I, ξ₁⟩⟨e^I, ξ₂⟩ ≥ 0, whose verification needs the Cauchy–Binet identity; only the property ξ̃₂ = σξ̃₁ a.e. on M₁ ∩ M₂ is used below.)

   c(x) := p₁θ₁(x)1_{M₁}(x) + p₂θ₂(x)(σ(x)1_{M₁∩M₂}(x) + 1_{M₂∖M₁}(x)),   ζ(x) := ξ̃₁(x) if x ∈ M₁, ζ(x) := ξ̃₂(x) otherwise.
c is Borel (ℤ is countable with the discrete σ-algebra; c is built from the Borel maps θ₁, θ₂, σ and the indicators of the Borel sets M₁, M₂), ζ is strongly measurable (piecewise on the Borel set M₁), c = 0 off A, and since at most one of 1_{M₁∩M₂}(x), 1_{M₂∖M₁}(x) is nonzero and |σ| = 1,
   (3a) |c(x)| ≤ |p₁|θ₁(x)1_{M₁}(x) + |p₂|θ₂(x)1_{M₂}(x) for all x.

4. Pointwise identity. Let x satisfy [x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ ⇒ ξ̃₂(x) = σ(x)ξ̃₁(x)]. Then p₁1_{M₁}(x)θ₁(x)ξ̃₁(x) + p₂1_{M₂}(x)θ₂(x)ξ̃₂(x) = c(x)ζ(x). Cases: if x ∉ A both sides are 0; if x ∈ M₁ ∖ M₂ both sides equal p₁θ₁(x)ξ̃₁(x); if x ∈ M₂ ∖ M₁ both sides equal p₂θ₂(x)ξ̃₂(x); if x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ the left side is p₁θ₁(x)ξ̃₁(x) + p₂θ₂(x)σ(x)ξ̃₁(x) = (p₁θ₁(x) + p₂θ₂(x)σ(x))ξ̃₁(x) = c(x)ζ(x).

5. Definition of R. Let M' := {x ∈ A : c(x) ≠ 0}, θ'(x) := |c(x)| ∈ ℕ and ξ'(x) := sgn(c(x))·ζ(x). Since |c|·sgn(c) = c, and c(x) = 0 whenever x ∉ M' (either x ∉ A, or x ∈ A with c(x) = 0), we have
   (5a) 1_{M'}(x)θ'(x)ξ'(x) = c(x)ζ(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P.

On K, f is ν-a.e.-strongly measurable (step 1) and ‖f‖ ≤ ‖F_1‖ + ‖F_2‖ ≤ Θ_1 + Θ_2 ν-a.e. (step 2), where Θ_1 + Θ_2 is ν-integrable on K (step 3); hence f is ν-integrable on K. (step 2), the bound being ν-integrable by step 3 with K = tsupport g (compact, ⊆ U).

Evaluation at α commutes with the Bochner integral (Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.integral_apply), and (g(x)f(x))(α) = h_1(x) − h_2(x); by (b) and (c), I(α) = ∫ h_1 dν − ∫ h_2 dν = T(ω_α) − T(ω_α) = 0. As α is arbitrary, I = 0.
6. (Fundamental lemma.) ℝ^P is a finite-dimensional real normed space with its Borel σ-algebra, Λ is a real Banach space, U is open, f is locally integrable on U with respect to ν (step 4), and ∫ g·f dν = 0 for every C^∞ function g with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ U (step 5). By Mathlib IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero, for ν-a.e. x, x ∈ U implies f(x) = 0.
